Date: 2026-10-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Proposed prepay schedule & frontloaded credits — Novus Health

Folks,

Novus Health (POC: Samira Khan) just signaled readiness to move to a multi-year prepay, but they need a frontloaded credit profile in year 1 to match their budget phasing. Key ask: 36-month commitment, $3.6M total committed value, with 60% of committed credits effective in year 1 (frontload) and the remaining distributed across years 2–3. To make the math work for them we proposed a blended term discount of 30% off list (vs our standard 18% for a comparable commit).

Why this is important:
- Novus is a strategically attractive customer (large health tech footprint, potential platform integration).
- They commit to a 36-month volume and want to standardize Redwood for inference across their product lines.

Risks / asks for approval:
- This is materially deeper than our standard term discount and shifts consumption to year 1. Finance, I need guidance on revenue recognition and reserve treatment.
- Legal: include an SLA and usage floors to limit churn risk.
- Sales leadership: approval to offer the 30% blended discount and frontloaded credits (document attached).

Attachments: Novus_Commit_Term_Sheet.pdf, Novus_pricing_model_2026Q4.xlsx

Proposed next step: internal sign-off today so I can send an updated term sheet and DocuSign link to Samira by COB.

Thanks,
Priyom
Priyom Das | Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-18T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed prepay schedule & frontloaded credits — Novus Health

Priyom,

Thanks for the context and the model. A few finance questions before we can authorize:

1) Revenue recognition impact: frontloading 60% in year 1 will create a sizable deferred balance and potential churn exposure. What % of usage do they anticipate to consume in Y1 vs reserved credits? The model assumes ~70% burn in year 1. Please confirm.

2) Credit liability: we need to set aside credit reserves for the unconsumed portion. I need to see a sensitivity table (best/worst/expected) for consumption over 12/24/36 months. Can you add that tab to the pricing model?

3) Discount cap: 30% blended is out of our standard delegated authority. Finance would prefer we cap to 25% and offset with contractual guardrails (use-based true-ups or incremental pricing tiers).

If Sales leadership confirms strategic value and Legal adds the SLA/true-up language, I'm OK taking this to CFO for one-off authorization.

-marissa
Marissa Cole | Head of Revenue Finance | Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-18T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed prepay schedule & frontloaded credits — Novus Health

Team,

I reviewed quickly — high level: Novus is priority (they're evaluating alternatives and have integration timelines tied to their product launch). I'm comfortable with a concession if we do the following:

- Maximum blended discount: 27.5% (midpoint between Finance and Sales).
- Add a 12-month usage floor (min 40% of frontloaded credits expected to be consumed in 12 months) with a true-up for under-consumption at a recovery rate of 50% of list price for the shortfall.
- Include a 60-day early-termination clawback on unused credits (drops to an annual true-up after month 12).
- Legal to prepare SLA + limited indemnity; Pricing ops to confirm rev recognition treatment.

If everyone agrees, Priyom — send the revised term sheet with these guardrails and I will escalate to CFO (Laura) for sole-exception approval. Please highlight strategic upsides in the escalation note (platform integration + marketplace potential).

-vivek
Vivek Kulkarni | SVP Sales | Redwood Inference
